Slice: Holds To Collect

Intent

The hold collector's to-do list: every hold whose holder has checked the tool out and whose hold hasn't yet been recorded collected. The collector works through it, so a holder's own checkout ends their hold as a Holds fact (Hold Collected) and the views about holds never infer it from the loan.

Trigger & Actor

  • Consumed by: the Hold Collector (Collect Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • What it lists: one row per hold that is live (placed, not cancelled, expired or collected) on a tool that its holder now has on loan. A row names the hold, its tool and holder, and the loan that collected it.

Read Model / View

  • View: Holds To Collect built from events: "Hold Placed", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled"
  • Consumed by: the Hold Collector (Collect Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A row appears shortly after the checkout is recorded and leaves shortly after Hold Collected is (seconds, not minutes).

HoldId, ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs.

Field Type Source / Notes
holdId HoldId Hold Placed.holdId.
toolId ToolId Hold Placed.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Hold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
loanId LoanId Derived: Tool Checked Out.loanId of the holder's open loan on the tool.

When a row appears. Tool Checked Out for a tool and neighbor who has a live hold on that tool creates the row for that hold (INV-HTC-1). A holder has at most one hold on a tool (INV-HOLD-2, Place Hold), so the checkout names at most one hold.

When a row leaves. Hold Collected for the hold (INV-HTC-2), or Hold Cancelled for it (INV-HTC-3): a hold cancelled in the moment between the checkout and the collector acting is never collected. Nothing puts a row back.

To know which holds are live, the view keeps, beyond its rows, every hold from Hold Placed until Hold Cancelled or Hold Collected for it. A hold that expired, or ended with its tool retired or lost, cannot be checked out by its holder (INV-CHK-3b, INV-CHK-4), so those endings need no rule here.

Queries

  • List holds to collect. Takes nothing. Returns every row with all four fields. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the collector.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-HTC-1: A hold joins the list when its holder's checkout of the tool is recorded.
    • Whether the hold was set aside (INV-CHK-3) or taken from the front of the queue before the set-aside was recorded (INV-CHK-3a) makes no difference: both are collections.
    • A checkout by a neighbor with no live hold on the tool adds nothing.
  • INV-HTC-2: Once Hold Collected is recorded for a hold, it leaves the list and never returns.
  • INV-HTC-3: A hold cancelled before it is collected leaves the list.
  • INV-HTC-4: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The list has no screen; only the Hold Collector reads it.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 is live on the cordless drill (T1).

  • Holder collects a set-aside (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and the list is empty
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, loan L5
    • Then: the list has H1: T1, Ben, L5.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: H1 is at the front of T1's queue, T1 has just been returned, and no Hold Fulfilled has been recorded
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, loan L6
    • Then: the list has H1: T1, Ben, L6.
  • Checkout with no hold (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: Ana has no hold on the hammer (T5)
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T5 and Ana
    • Then: the list is unchanged.
  • Someone else's checkout (INV-HTC-1)
    • Given: H1 is live on T1 and Cara, who has no hold on it, is allowed to take it (no set-aside and Ben not at the front: INV-CHK-3a does not apply)
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Cara
    • Then: the list is unchanged.
  • Hold collected (INV-HTC-2)
    • Given: the list has H1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Cancelled before collection (INV-HTC-3)
    • Given: the list has H1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: the list is empty.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-HTC-4)
    • Given: the list has H1 once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out is applied again
    • Then: the list still has H1 once.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-HTC-4).
  • Events for a hold no longer listed: once a row has left, a later Hold Collected or Hold Cancelled for it changes nothing.
  • The collector reads a row twice before Hold Collected lands: the list may return the same hold on two reads in a row. Collecting a hold once is Collect Hold's rule, enforced when it runs; the list need not prevent the second read.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: internal; no caller outside the Hold Collector reads it.
  • PII & compliance: ids only.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold, and the Hold Cancelled recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account): holdId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/cancel-hold.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Hold Collector reads it and issues Collect Hold.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":1,"name":"Collect Hold","x0":274.25,"x1":418.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: Collect Hold

Intent

When a holder checks out the tool they hold, record that their hold was collected, so the hold ends as a Holds fact and the views about holds hear it from their own context. Checking out records only Tool Checked Out; Hold Collected is recorded separately, by this slice. The system does this itself; no person collects a hold.

What follows a collection is decided by the slices that read Hold Collected: the hold leaves My Holds, Holds To Fulfill's queue, Pickup Notices To Send and Pickups To Expire, and a failed pickup email for it leaves Undelivered Notices.

Trigger & Actor

  • Pattern: automation. The Hold Collector, a system processor, watches the Holds To Collect list (slices/holds-to-collect.md). Only the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold; it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • Triggering condition: a hold is on the list: its holder has an open loan on its tool.
  • When it acts: the list changes only when a checkout lands, so the collector acts whenever the list changes, on each item that appears.
  • What it does: it issues Collect Hold for the item's hold and loan. If the command is refused or is a repeat, nothing is recorded and the processor moves on.

Command / Input

Command: Collect Hold

HoldId and LoanId are UUIDs.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
holdId HoldId yes The hold collected. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-COL-5) and is still live (INV-COL-2).
loanId LoanId yes The loan that collected it, from the list item: the holder's open loan on the hold's tool (INV-COL-3).

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Hold Collector, also in this slice, reading Holds To Collect.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Collected → context Holds Read by: Holds To Collect (the hold leaves the list), My Holds (the hold drops off), Holds To Fulfill (the hold leaves the queue), Pickup Notices To Send and Pickups To Expire (the set-aside ends), Undelivered Notices (a pickup-notice entry drops off).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes Set by the system: the tool on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborId NeighborId yes Set by the system: the holder on the hold's Hold Placed.
loanId LoanId yes From the command: the loan that collected the hold.
collectedAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Collected takes the hold off Holds To Collect, My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-COL-1: Only the Hold Collector collects holds, and only from Holds To Collect.
  • INV-COL-2: A hold is collected only while it is live: placed, and not cancelled, expired or already collected.
    • A hold cancelled in the moment between the checkout and the collector acting is refused hold-ended, and stays ended.
  • INV-COL-3: The loan named must be the holder's open loan on the hold's tool.
    • The collector takes it from the list item; a different loan is a faulty caller.
  • INV-COL-4: Collecting a hold already collected succeeds and records nothing.
  • INV-COL-5: The hold must exist.
  • INV-COL-6: Collect Hold records only Hold Collected.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 is live on the cordless drill (T1), and Tool Checked Out was recorded for T1 and Ben as loan L5.

  • Happy path (INV-COL-1, INV-COL-3, INV-COL-6)
    • Given: H1 is on Holds To Collect with loan L5
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: Hold Collected is recorded for H1: tool T1, holder Ben, loan L5, and the moment. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Front hold collected before the set-aside (INV-COL-2)
    • Given: H1 was never fulfilled; Ben took T1 from the front of the queue
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: Hold Collected is recorded for H1.
  • Collected twice (INV-COL-4)
    • Given: Hold Collected has been recorded for H1
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Cancelled before the collector acts (INV-COL-2)
    • Given: Hold Cancelled was recorded for H1 after the checkout
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Wrong loan (INV-COL-3)
    • Given: H1 is on the list with loan L5
    • When: Collect Hold arrives for H1 and L9
    • Then: refused with loan-mismatch. No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-COL-5)
    • Given: no hold has ID H9
    • When: Collect Hold arrives for H9
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found. No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing. No person sees these reasons; they are logged with the hold ID. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-COL-5).
  2. If Hold Collected is already recorded for the hold, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-COL-4).
  3. hold-ended (INV-COL-2).
  4. loan-mismatch (INV-COL-3).
Reason Sentence Rule
hold-not-found There is no such hold. INV-COL-5
hold-ended This hold has already ended. INV-COL-2
loan-mismatch This loan did not collect this hold. INV-COL-3

hold-not-found and hold-ended mean the same conditions as in Cancel Hold. A missing or malformed hold ID or loan ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a collection is identified by its hold. A repeat after Hold Collected succeeds and records nothing. The collector may read the same item twice before Hold Collected lands; the second attempt is the repeat above.

Requests at the same moment: Collect Hold is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold, so at most one Hold Collected is recorded for a hold.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: internal; only the Hold Collector issues it (INV-COL-1).
  • PII & compliance: ids and a time only.
  • Performance / SLA: a hold is collected shortly after its checkout lands (seconds, not minutes); until then the hold views still show it, as the doc of each says.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold and the slices that repeat it), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (this slice): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, slices/cancel-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Holds To Collect (slices/holds-to-collect.md).
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Holds To Collect, My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices.

Open Questions

None.
